title: Criterion 0 noise floor, cross-frame re-grade of A's five cuts, and the arithmetic that does not retire the residue

rule_compliance.no_confirmation_without_a_named_instrume: every finding below carries instrument + protocol fields; findings without them are labelled OPEN, not confirmed

correction_to_the_premise.claim_received: 383 fresh single + 3 x 135 MB per additional panel = 788, therefore the residue may not exist
correction_to_the_premise.status: the arithmetic is sound and it explains the PEAK; it does not touch the residue, which is a FLOOR measurement
why: 135 MB/panel explains the reading WHILE four panels are open. The residue claim has never been about that reading.

The residue is measured after the multichart is collapsed back to a single chart and garbage collection is forced: at the sample instant there is one chart, so a per-panel cost term cannot contribute to it.
On the cross-frame gauge the collapsed floors climb monotonically 74.06 -> 86.91 -> 100.10 -> 115.56 MB across four cycles. Additional-panel cost is zero at every one of those samples.
correction_to_the_premise.instrument: Performance.getMetrics JSHeapUsedSize (the Performance Monitor figure), sampled after two forced collectGarbage calls with the multichart collapsed to a single chart
correction_to_the_premise.settle_protocol: collapse to single chart, 2 x HeapProfiler.collectGarbage with 400ms between, then sample
correction_to_the_premise.residue_status: STILL PRESENT on the cross-frame gauge. Not retired by the peak arithmetic.

job_1_criterion_0.instrument: Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Documents, Frames, Nodes, JSEventListeners); performance.memory reported alongside, never instead
job_1_criterion_0.settle_protocol: one fresh page per load, cache disabled, harness boot path, wait until window.chart.data.length > 200, forced GC, then sample; identical every load
job_1_criterion_0.surface: deployed dist-v9 single chart, 1 frame / 2 documents (NOT the PO's 11-18 document surface)
job_1_criterion_0.devtools: no DevTools window; CDP attached, and nothing but booleans and numbers crosses the bridge, so the W81 console-retention mechanism is not in these figures

the_number_that_matters.reading: the residue is nineteen times the between-session noise floor on this surface. It is not a noise artefact.

two_different_noises_must_not_be_conflat.between_session_fresh_load_spread: 0.73 MB — small; this is what Criterion 0 measures
two_different_noises_must_not_be_conflat.within_run_per_delta_sd: 4.1 MB (W83) — large; this is what swamped the A-versus-B comparison
two_different_noises_must_not_be_conflat.consequence: the residue clears its noise floor by 19x AND the A/B difference sits inside its noise floor. Both are true; they are different variances.

document_count_is_deterministic_here.observed: 2 documents on all ten loads, spread 0, and 1 frame on all ten
document_count_is_deterministic_here.consequence: the PO's 13-versus-18 nondeterminism does not exist on the bare chart shell. It lives in the surrounding app, the saved layout, or the browser profile — not in the chart.

job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.why_re_graded: the W84 retraction was measured on performance.memory. If that gauge were blind to panel realms the grade would be void, so the grade has been recomputed on the cross-frame gauge the Director specified.
job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.instrument: Performance.getMetrics JSHeapUsedSize at the same instant as every performance.memory sample (recorded since W86)
job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.settle_protocol: collapsed single-chart floor, 2 x forced GC, distinct datasets, 4 cycles
job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.verdict: the cuts do not measure smaller on the cross-frame gauge either: 13.83 with them ON against 12.77 with them OFF, i.e. 1.06 MB/cycle WORSE, well inside the per-delta noise.
job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.n: one run per arm, three deltas each. This does not write the cuts off and I am not writing them off — it says the cross-frame gauge does not rescue them. Settling it needs ~12 runs per arm at the measured per-delta sd (W83 resolution figure).
job_3_cross_frame_regrade_of_As_five_cut.what_changed_and_what_did_not: the gauge changed the MAGNITUDE (see below) but not the SIGN of the comparison. The W84 retraction stands on the gauge the Director asked for.

gauge_reconciliation_the_significant_fin.on_absolutes: b/a = 0.82 (61.52 vs 75.40 median at the fresh floor) — a 1.22x disagreement
gauge_reconciliation_the_significant_fin.on_deltas: a/b = 1.76x to 2.00x — performance.memory reports roughly DOUBLE the per-cycle growth that Performance Monitor reports
gauge_reconciliation_the_significant_fin.consequence: my headline 24 MB/cycle and the PO's hand-measured ~12 MB/cycle are the same measurement read on two gauges. On the Director's chosen gauge my harness reads 13.83 +/- 1.42 MB/cycle against the PO's ~12. THE TWENTY-FOLD CALIBRATION GAP IS CLOSED, and it closes without any surface correction.
gauge_reconciliation_the_significant_fin.restatement_owed: every per-cycle figure I have reported on performance.memory should be halved to compare with a Performance Monitor reading. 23.5 pre-fix becomes ~13. I am restating rather than defending.

leading_candidate_checked_in_source.candidate: panel construction gated on the failing /api/chart/preferences response (advisor's H5-is-the-same-bug hypothesis)
leading_candidate_checked_in_source.finding: NOT SUPPORTED by the source. /api/chart/preferences is touched only in v9ChartTemplatesStorage.js, in hydrateV9ChartTemplatesFromCloud (GET) and syncV9ChartTemplatesCloudDirect (POST). The GET path returns local templates on !res.ok and on throw; the POST path returns false. Neither blocks, retries, or gates construction, and MultichartGrid.jsx contains no reference to preferencesSync at all.
leading_candidate_checked_in_source.instrument: source read of v9ChartTemplatesStorage.js lines 89-140 and a preferencesSync grep across MultichartGrid.jsx
leading_candidate_checked_in_source.caveat: this rules out template hydration as the gate. It does not rule out a different consumer on the PO's surface, which I cannot see without the route.
leading_candidate_checked_in_source.no_re_measurement_of_Bs_500: confirmed — I did not issue a single request to that endpoint

job_2_name_the_383_mb.why_not_retained_size: self size answers the question actually posed — Object/Array dominating means bar data held as JS objects, Float64Array means already columnar, HeapNumber means boxed doubles. Retained size answers OWNERSHIP, which REALM-SURVIVAL-V1 and the retainer-path aggregation already answer. Substituting one for the other silently is the error I am avoiding by naming it.
job_2_name_the_383_mb.surface_caveat_stated_before_the_result: this snapshots MY 61 MB / 2-document floor, not the PO's 383 MB / 11-18 document floor. Composition proportions may transfer; the absolute mass does not. Naming the PO's 383 MB requires the route.
